extracted.intended_audience: Christian readers seeking spiritual growth (monastics, devout laypersons, clergy)
extracted.subtask_description: A chaptered devotional manual giving prescriptive guidance for living a Christian, penitential, and contemplative life — describing signs of grace vs. nature, duties (solitude, mortification, humility), and attitudes toward suffering and divine mysteries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid mixture of grace with earthly consolations
rubrics_metrics.description: Grace is of great price and does not tolerate being mixed with foreign things or terrestrial consolations; remove whatever hinders its spread.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you desire grace to fructify, set aside earthly comforts and pleasures; count the world as nothing and occupy yourself with God rather than outward works. Withdraw from company when necessary so the soul can pour itself out before God in fervent prayer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek solitude and secret prayer
rubrics_metrics.description: Retire to a secret place, love to remain alone, and avoid seeking the conversation of others so the soul may pour itself out to God in fervent prayer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solitude preserves compunction and a pure conscience; the inward life requires withdrawal from external entertainments and frequent private prayer to maintain spiritual progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detach from friends and worldly consolations
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate yourself from acquaintances and friends and wean your soul from all earthly consolation if you desire grace to spread within you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detachment means being free from worldly attachments so the heart can be wholly for God; such detachment brings confidence at the hour of death and inner liberty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mortify inclinations and uproot self-love
rubrics_metrics.description: To attain high perfection one must begin courageously and 'put the axe to the root' to uproot even hidden remains of disordered self-love and desires for sensible goods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Almost all vices spring from disordered self-love; perfect victory is to triumph over oneself so the senses obey reason and the person becomes master of themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discern movements of nature versus grace
rubrics_metrics.description: Observe carefully the movements of nature and grace, since they are often opposed and can be hard to distinguish even for the spiritually enlightened.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop discernment; not every apparent good comes from grace—nature can imitate good. Examine motives and tendencies to see whether an inclination tends to self or to God.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature attracts by artifice; grace acts with simplicity
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature is full of artifice, attraction and self-end; grace acts simply and avoids even the least appearance of evil, doing all for God alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer simplicity of intention and action; suspect cleverness and self-seeking even when deeds look attractive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature resists mortification; grace seeks to be mortified
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature recoils from being conquered and submitting, while grace inclines one to mortify oneself, resist sensuality, and desire to be humbled and dependent on God.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test interior movements by their openness to self-denial and willingness to be 'defeated' for God rather than to assert freedom or domination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature acts for self-interest; grace for the common good
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature works for its own advantage and calculates gain; grace considers what may be useful to many and is not preoccupied with personal profit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate acts by whether they seek praise or profit for self, or the welfare and salvation of others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature loves honors; grace gives glory to God
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature loves to receive respect and honors; grace faithfully renders all honor and glory to God alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humility and attribution of credit to God indicate grace; craving for recognition signals natural self-interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature fears contempt; grace rejoices in suffering for Christ
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature fears confusion and contempt; grace rejoices to suffer outrages for the name of Jesus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A willingness to endure dishonor for Christ's sake is a sign of grace; avoidance of suffering out of pride indicates nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature loves ease; grace delights in labor
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature loves bodily rest and idleness; grace cannot be idle and finds joy in work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active charity and tireless service are marks of grace; desire for leisure and ease may indicate natural tendencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature prefers beauty and curiosity; grace prefers simplicity and humility
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature seeks curious and beautiful things and rejects what is coarse; grace delights in the simple and humble and will clothe itself in rags if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer humble, simple exercises and settings as signs of grace; attraction to novelty and elegance can mask self-seeking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature attaches to temporal goods; grace seeks eternal goods
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature covets temporal goods and is troubled by loss; grace aspires only to eternal goods and is unattached to earthly losses or insults.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure attachments by steadiness in the face of loss—if peace remains, grace likely predominates; if agitation arises, nature may be in control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature is acquisitive; grace is generous and gives freely
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature loves to receive and keep what is its own; grace is generous, avoids singularity, and believes it is more blessed to give than to receive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generosity without seeking return is a fruit of grace; hoarding and self-preservation are signs of nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature seeks outward display; grace withdraws from appearance
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature tends toward creatures and outward display; grace elevates toward God, excites to virtue, renounces the world and blushes to appear before men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A person who seeks to conceal virtues and avoid public commendation likely acts from grace; ostentation points to nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature seeks external consolation; grace seeks consolation in God alone
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature rejoices in outward consolation that flatters the senses; grace seeks consolation only in God and sets delights in the sovereign good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Satisfaction drawn primarily from prayer and union with God indicates grace; dependence on external comforts indicates nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature expects recompense; grace desires God alone as reward
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature acts for gain and hopes to obtain something equal or better in return; grace wants God alone and seeks temporal goods only as means to eternal goods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acts done solely for God's glory, without expectation of worldly reward, are signs of grace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature values numbers, rank and lineage; grace loves enemies and values virtue
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature delights in many friends, high rank, and noble birth; grace loves enemies, is not proud of numbers, and prefers the virtuous poor to the rich.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for the humble and exercise of charity toward enemies indicate grace; social climbing and favoritism signal nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature complains at lack; grace bears poverty with constancy
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature is quick to complain at what it lacks; grace endures poverty with constancy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peaceful endurance in want and simplicity in provision mark grace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature centers things on itself; grace refers all to God
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature reports everything to itself and contends for its interests; grace brings everything back to God, claiming no good for itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A spirit that attributes goods to God and submits thoughts to divine wisdom evidences grace; self-justifying attitudes suggest nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature is inquisitive and ostentatious; grace represses curiosity and ostentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature desires secrets and novelty to be known and admired; grace does not concern itself with the new or curious and represses vainglory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid seeking novelty for its own sake; prefer humble obscurity and silent charity as signs of grace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grace is the supernatural seal of the elect
rubrics_metrics.description: Grace is a supernatural light and special gift of God; it is the sign by which the elect are known and the pledge of eternal salvation, elevating man toward heavenly goods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The more nature is weakened and subdued, the more grace spreads and restores the image of God within; regular reception of grace leads to growth in virtue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize human weakness and the need for divine grace
rubrics_metrics.description: Because of original sin the natural powers are insufficient; one feels the law of sin in the flesh and needs a great grace to overcome inclinations to evil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge the inability to do good without grace; cultivate prayerful dependence and humility rather than self-confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grace is necessary to begin, continue, and complete good works
rubrics_metrics.description: Without divine grace a person can do nothing; grace is needed to start the good, to preserve it, and to bring it to perfection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pray for continual infusions of grace each morning; do not trust solely in natural gifts, intelligence, or virtues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural gifts have no value without grace
rubrics_metrics.description: Arts, riches, beauty, strength, genius, eloquence and even faith are nothing in God's eyes without grace and charity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess gifts by whether they are accompanied by charity and humility; prioritize interior sanctity over external talents or achievements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renounce yourself and imitate Christ by bearing the Cross
rubrics_metrics.description: You enter into Christ only by going out of yourself; follow Christ as the way, truth and life, renounce yourself, bear the cross, and be prepared to die to self.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice self-renunciation, poverty of spirit, humility, and readiness to accept contempt or suffering as participation in Christ's cross.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obey Christ's commands as the path to truth and life
rubrics_metrics.description: If you wish for life, keep Christ's commandments; if you wish to be perfect, sell all; if you wish to be Christ's disciple, renounce yourself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete obedience and decisive renunciation of attachments are expected marks of discipleship; the cross is not optional for true followers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persevere in carrying the Cross together with courage
rubrics_metrics.description: Having taken up the cross, continue to carry it courageously; the life of the religious is a cross that leads to glory, and one must not abandon it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage mutual support among brethren; expect trials and be ready to die generously in this spiritual warfare rather than flee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond to faults with patience and humility, not excessive despondency
rubrics_metrics.description: Patience and humility in trials are more pleasing than much joy and fervor in prosperity; do not be unduly troubled by light faults but seek pardon and recover quietly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When surprised by faults, recover promptly, avoid harsh words that scandalize the weak, and rely on God's help; excessive self-accusation often springs from pride rather than true contrition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bear trials with constancy and prepare for further suffering
rubrics_metrics.description: Arm yourself with perseverance and prepare to endure more; you are human and will fall—God sustains and raises those who acknowledge their infirmity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See trials as means of salvation; ask God for a good end and trust in his living word for consolation and renewal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not pry into God's hidden judgments or the comparative merits of saints
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid disputing about high subjects and hidden judgments of God (why one is abandoned and another favored) or about which saint is greater; these are beyond human intelligence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When tempted to question divine judgments, respond: 'You are just, Lord, and your judgments are right.' Focus on one's own sanctification rather than speculative comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refrain from vain curiosity about the heavenly order; cultivate humility
rubrics_metrics.description: Speculations about who is greatest in heaven produce disputes, pride and jealousy; they are sterile and displeasing to the saints who prefer humility and praise of God.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pray with tears and fervor for the saints' intercession instead of seeking to rank them; imitation and humility are more profitable than curiosities about the heavenly hierarchy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer to labor for your salvation rather than search for hidden mysteries
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not occupy yourself with questions above your intelligence; think continually of what God prescribes and keep to duties—there is enough to account for in one's own works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Channel energies into prayer, penance, and virtuous works rather than speculative inquiry into divine secrets; humility and practical obedience are the path to salvation.
